content:
Two deadlines are converging in Webb County today. Early in-person voting has reached its fifth day and enters the home stretch, and Friday, October 23 is the last day to apply for a ballot by mail in the November 3 joint general election.

The Webb County Elections Office reports that 13,723 ballots had been cast through the third day of early voting, according to figures published October 21 by SignalNews Laredo, based on reporting by KGNS. That total comprised 13,225 in-person votes and 498 mail ballots.

Statewide, the pace is extraordinary. Texas Secretary of State figures cited by The Directory News showed 1,934,269 Texans had voted early through Wednesday — about 10.2 percent of the state’s more than 19 million registered voters — with Texas running roughly 74 percent ahead of its 2022 pace at the same point. A separate statewide tracker from Transparency USA reported approximately 2.28 million ballots cast as of October 22 at 2:10 p.m. Central Time, with 242 of Texas’s 254 counties reporting. Those figures are provisional and incomplete, and some counties, including Webb, lag in uploading their data — so any county-by-county comparison should be treated as a snapshot, not a final verdict.

What’s on the Webb County ballot

This is one of the busiest ballots in recent local memory. Voters are choosing a new mayor of Laredo, with incumbent Víctor Treviño facing challengers including Alfonso “Poncho” Casso, Jose “JD” Gonzalez, Alyssa Cigarroa and Jorge Garza, plus city council seats, school board races, and the high-profile Texas 28th District congressional contest between incumbent Democrat Henry Cuellar and Republican challenger Tano Tijerina. The state ballot also includes the U.S. Senate race between James Talarico and Ken Paxton and several propositions that can make the ballot longer than usual.

The deadlines that matter now

  • Today, Friday, October 23: last day to apply for a ballot by mail. The application must be received at PO Box 233 — a postmark is not enough.
  • Friday, October 30: last day of early voting.
  • Tuesday, November 3: Election Day. Mail ballots must be received at PO Box 233 and postmarked by the post office clerk on Election Day, or hand-delivered by the voter to the Elections Office by 7 p.m.

The county operates countywide vote centers for early voting, and there are 14 early voting locations. The Elections Office is at 720 Convent Ave. in Laredo, phone (956) 523-4050. Webb Watch previously covered the record opening-day pace of early voting; the question now is whether the second half of the early voting period holds that momentum through October 30.

title: Early Voting Enters the Home Stretch in Webb County — and Today Is the Last Day to Apply for a Mail Ballot
